result.title: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs
result.summary: Federated fine-tuning enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to collaboratively adapt to distributed private data. However, long-context fine-tuning on resource-constrained devices faces substantial challenges arising from excessive activation memory, heterogeneous token-importance patterns across clients, and communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose SMELL, a Sparsity-aware and Memory-Efficient federated fine-tuning framework for Long-context LLMs. SMELL integrates three complementary mechanisms: Local Sparse-Forward Adaptation (LSFA), Consensus-Anchored Sparsity Coordination (CASC), and Communication-Efficient Progressive Update Recovery (CPUR). These mechanisms jointly enable memory-efficient local adaptation, heterogeneity-aware sparsity coordination, and lightweight model-update transmission. Experiments on OPT-350M and LLaMA2-7B demonstrate that SMELL reduces peak memory consumption by up to 88.35% compared with conventional fine-tuning and 13.25% compared with forward-only LoRA fine-tuning at a 16K context length. Furthermore, SMELL improves fine-tuning performance under certain non-IID settings and supports compact update transmission with progressive reconstruction, demonstrating its potential for resource-efficient federated long-context LLM adaptation.
